question: Given that only 4.7% of each document's slots survive later writes, does MT acquisition actually improve as documents 2..16 are written -- or is the 16-document cartridge worth about one document?
variable_under_test: number of documents written, k = 0..16 (the per-document cache snapshots of the canonical top-32 run; nothing else varies -- no training, no config change, no code change)
baseline_ref: EXP-007-top32 / ORACLE-WRITE control (standalone-eval convention QA 2.1771795749664307 / MT 2.5524158477783203) as the k=16 correctness gate; Phase-1 cache (QA 2.23880672454834 / MT 3.7825491428375244) as the k=0 anchor

diagnostics.verdict_on_the_dispatched_dichotomy: MT improves steadily with k -- the 'writing 16 documents is worth about one document' branch is REFUTED. MT after doc 1 (3.7446) is 1.192 WORSE than MT after doc 16 (2.5524); doc 1 alone accounts for 3.1% of the total k=0 -> k=16 MT drop, documents 2..16 for 96.9%.
diagnostics.curve_shape: strictly monotone DECREASING from k=0 to k=12 (verified for every one of the 12 steps), minimum MT = 2.4352 at k=12, then strictly monotone INCREASING for k=13,14,15,16 (2.4488, 2.4546, 2.5004, 2.5524).

early_gain_is_disproportionate.note: documents 1-3 hold 18.8% of the MT eval questions but deliver 56.7% of the total MT improvement, so a large part of the early gain is a global MT-distribution/format shift rather than per-document content acquisition

tail_degradation.note: documents 13-16 carry 27.5% of the MT eval questions, yet writing them makes MT monotonically WORSE by +0.117 -- the overwrite signature appears only in the tail

eval_coverage_MT.method: metadata-level: qasper_eval_MT.parquet metadata.title joined against the 16 document_key() titles in the write order produced by group_conversations_by_document(qwen_qasper_MT_task_8192.parquet); 16/16 matched, 0 unmatched

eval_coverage_QA.note: the QA (forgetting) eval papers are entirely disjoint from the 16 Phase-2 documents

curve_vs_models.sign_of_residual: negative for k=2..15 (observed MT is BELOW the linear-accumulation prediction), i.e. the real curve is front-loaded and then saturates

correctness_gate.note: both anchors reproduce ORACLE-WRITE's standalone-eval numbers to all 16 printed digits

mass_on_S.new_measurement: none -- this task performed NO AM solve (eval-only on snapshots the canonical run already wrote)

command: bash research_loop/results/DIAG-SEQUENCE/launch_diag_sequence.sh  (34 standalone evals: examples/qasper2/train/eval_forgetting.py with CHECKPOINT_PATH = each cache-after-doc-*.pt of the canonical DIAG-OVERWRITE run plus the Phase-1 cache, EVAL_DATA_PATH = data/qasper/eval/qasper_eval_{QA,MT}.parquet, MODEL_NAME=Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507, BATCH_SIZE=4 default, RUN_NAME=DIAG-SEQUENCE_doc<k>_<split>, WANDB_GROUP=B-OVERWRITE, WANDB_DISABLED=0; 'Eval loss' parsed from the log then the PID killed per RUNBOOK 1) ; then research_loop/results/DIAG-SEQUENCE/finalize.py (curve assembly, wandb summary run, `diagnostic` tag applied to all 34 per-eval runs via the wandb API). NO training was run and NO source file was edited. Imports pinned to the frozen snapshot /tmp/amsnap_seq (git archive HEAD {cartridges,examples} at HEAD=06cd28c93fa4aa1daa1e3d5faaed1ae72c8ae218; manifest sha256 dfc10ac9600bfe51db7137595506ddad388d22cac6b4668cd05766b861d90a95, re-verified byte-identical after the run; HEAD also unchanged); CARTRIDGES_DIR pinned at the snapshot; the eval driver itself was executed from the snapshot; cartridges.__file__ = /tmp/amsnap_seq/cartridges printed from cwd=/tmp in the job log. One GPU (index 0) claimed via flock.
observations: The artefacts already existed -- the canonical DIAG-OVERWRITE run saved a full cache snapshot after every document (SAVE_AFTER_EACH_DOCUMENT=1), all 16 present -- so this was 34 standalone evals and no training. Correctness gate passed exactly: the doc-16 snapshot gives QA 2.1771795749664307 / MT 2.5524158477783203, matching the ORACLE-WRITE control to all 16 printed digits, and the Phase-1 anchors reproduce 2.23880672454834 / 3.7825491428375244 likewise; every eval log shows the intended checkpoint path. THE 'ONE DOCUMENT' BRANCH IS REFUTED: MT after document 1 is 3.7446, only 0.038 below the Phase-1 3.7825 and 1.192 WORSE than the 16-document 2.5524; document 1 alone accounts for 3.1% of the total MT drop and documents 2..16 for 96.9%. THE RESULT IS THE MIDDLE BRANCH: MT falls strictly monotonically at every step from k=0 to k=12 (3.7825, 3.7445, 3.3669, 3.0848, 3.0338, 2.9645, 2.8945, 2.8085, 2.7099, 2.7056, 2.5332, 2.4864, 2.4352), reaches its minimum 2.4352 at k=12, and then rises strictly monotonically over the last four documents to 2.5524 -- a +0.117 regression from the best point, so the effective document capacity of this configuration is about 12. The tail degradation is not a coverage artefact: documents 13-16 carry 27.5% of the MT eval questions (19 of 69) and writing them still makes MT monotonically worse. The gain is also strongly front-loaded: documents 1-3 hold only 18.8% of the eval questions but deliver 56.7% of the total MT improvement, so part of the early movement is a global MT-distribution shift rather than per-document content acquisition, and the observed curve sits below a linear-accumulation prediction for every k in 2..15 (mean |residual| 0.345). QA behaves the same way one step later: it drops below the untouched Phase-1 floor at every k from 1 to 16, bottoms at 2.0239 at k=13, then regresses +0.153 to 2.1772 at k=16. On the eval-coverage question: the MT eval set is spread across ALL 16 training documents (69 examples, 16 unique paper_ids matched 16/16 by title against the write order, 3-7 questions each, cumulative coverage near-linear in k), and the QA eval's 16 papers are entirely disjoint from the 16 Phase-2 documents. Caveats: the eval splits are tiny (MT n=5 batches / 69 examples, QA n=6 / 78), so single-step deltas below ~0.15 -- which includes the marginal effect of most individual documents and the whole k=12..16 tail regression -- sit at or inside the noise band; only the large-scale shape (k=0 to k=12) is far outside it. All 17 snapshots come from one run at one seed, so the curve is a single realisation and the saturation point k=12 is not seed-varied. Per-document marginal deltas correlate only weakly with per-document eval share (Spearman 0.51 over 16 points). No AM solve was performed here, so no new mass_on_S exists; the source run's values (0.15851 solve-side, 0.08961 MT / 0.08272 QA eval-time on the written union) are recorded in diagnostics as inherited.
